rubrics.justification: Describes the embryo as an expanded blastocyst with compact ICM, cohesive TE, and thinned zona, which is consistent with the provided 3AA grade; appropriately notes single-image limitations, though some image-specific details may be slightly inferential.
Strong integration of age, thin endometrium, BMI, alcohol use, male factor, first cycle status, and sperm parameters with embryo quality and prognosis.
Final assessment is generally logical, but the response contains internal inconsistency in probability estimates and some hedging/contradictory ranges before settling on 20–30%.

Largely aligned with Gardner grading principles and standard IVF practice, including emphasis on single embryo transfer and caution about thin endometrium; minor deviations include speculative treatment suggestions and somewhat imprecise success-rate framing.

Provides some practical guidance such as single embryo transfer and future consideration of lining optimization/lifestyle changes, but recommendations are not highly specific or operationalized for this exact case.
